'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Al-Shifa Hospital siege]]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces]] detain Mohammad abu Salmiya, the director of the [[Al-Shifa Hospital]], and several doctors working under him, after a convoy belonging to the [[World Health Organization]] was stopped by [[Israeli soldier]]s. [[Israel]] accuses the director and the doctors of having sheltered [[Hamas]] fighters in the hospital. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/nov/23/israels-army-arrests-gaza-hospital-director-and-bombs-300-targets-amid-truce-delay (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***[[CENTCOM]] reports that the [[USS Thomas Hudner|USS ''Thomas Hudner'']] has shot down "multiple" Israel-bound [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|attack drones]] launched from [[Houthi]]-controlled [[Yemen]] over the [[Red Sea]]. No injuries or damage are reported. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/4324690-us-warship-attack-drones-red-sea/ (''The Hill'')]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Southern Ukraine campaign]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[cluster munition]] strike in [[Chornobaivka]], [[Kherson Raion|Kherson]], kills at least three [[civilian]]s. Five people are also injured by Russian [[artillery]] [[shell (projectile)|shelling]] with more than 60 residential buildings reportedly damaged. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/ukraine-3-civilians-killed-russian-shelling-russia-drone-105121065 (AP via ABC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Modern immigration to the United Kingdom]]
**The [[Office for National Statistics]] reports that [[net migration rate|net migration]] to the [[United Kingdom]] reached a record of 745,000 in 2022, with the vast majority of arrivals being from non-[[European Union|EU]] countries. [https://news.sky.com/story/net-migration-rose-to-672-000-in-year-to-june-up-from-607-000-in-the-previous-year-latest-ons-figures-show-13013846 (Sky News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2023 Chinese pneumonia outbreak]]
**The [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) reports that [[Chinese authorities]] have not detected any unusual or new [[pathogen]]s in the recent increase of [[respiratory disease]]s among children in [[northern China]]. The WHO continues to monitor the situation. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/china-reports-no-unusual-pathogens-in-respiratory-illness-surge-who-4601367 (AFP via NDTV)]
*[[Mpox in the Democratic Republic of the Congo]]
**The [[World Health Organization]] reports the first sexual transmission case of [[mpox]] in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] in a [[Belgium]] resident who traveled there. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/11/24/who-confirms-monkeypox-spreads-sexually-in-dr-congo-amid-outbreak (Al Jazeera)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Japan–South Korea relations]]
**The [[Judiciary of South Korea#High Courts and District Courts|High Court]] of [[Seoul]], [[South Korea]], orders [[Japan]] to pay compensation of [[South Korean won|₩]]200 million (around {{JPY|22 million|link=yes}} or [[United States dollar|US$]]154,000) to 16 [[comfort women]], overturning a previous ruling that denied the women's claims due to [[sovereign immunity]]. [https://mb.com.ph/2023/11/23/s-korea-court-rules-in-favour-of-victims-of-wartime-sexual-slavery (AFP via ''Manila Bulletin'')]
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[North Korea]] terminates its [[Peace Treaty on Korean Peninsula|2018 agreement]] with South Korea, citing escalations in military provocations as well as plans to deploy [[Korean People's Army|military forces]] along the [[Military Demarcation Line]]. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2023/11/23/north-korea-suspends-military-accord-with-south-after-satellite-launch_6280043_4.html (AFP via ''Le Monde'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 Dublin riot]]
**[[Riot]]ing occurs in [[Dublin]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], following a [[mass stabbing]] outside a school which injured a woman and three children. [[Garda Commissioner]] [[Drew Harris]] blames "[[far-right politics|far-right]] [[hooligan]]s" for the unrest. [https://apnews.com/article/dublin-ireland-stabbing-children-9a75c71fbac34fe789220c684c5eb661 (AP)]
*[[Chad]]'s [[National Transitional Council (Chad)|junta parliament]] approves an [[amnesty]] law, terminating [[prosecution]]s and [[conviction]]s related to the [[2022 Chadian protests|2022 anti-government protest]] deaths. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/chad-grants-general-amnesty-ending-prosecution-verdicts-over-deaths-of-protesters-in-2022-anti-govt-rally-101700765876416.html (AFP via ''Hindustan Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war protests]]
**Pro-[[State of Palestine|Palestine]] protesters disrupt the [[Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade]] in [[New York City]], [[United States]], minutes after the start of the parade. The parade resumes after the protesters are taken into custody. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/US/pro-palestinian-protesters-force-macys-thanksgiving-day-temporarily/story?id=105124720 (ABC News)]
**[[Cubans]] hold a pro-Palestine protest at the [[Embassy of the United States, Havana|Embassy of the United States]] in [[Havana]], [[Cuba]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/cuba-stages-pro-palestine-march-past-us-embassy-havana-2023-11-23/ (Reuters)]
